messages.text: hi sarah, is about the small fans

Hi, I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed your fan question to me.

To help with the small fans, I need two things:

1. Which miner is it? (for example NerdQX, Bitaxe, Magic M. 40T)
2. What are the fans doing? Are they not spinning, loud, rattling, or running at the wrong speed? Is anything showing on the screen or in the web UI?

If it's easier, you can send a photo or a short video of the fans running.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks for the photo. It shows the black power supply brick with its small fan on the end, plugged in by the barrel cable. Behind it is your miner on the green stand, with its big blue-lit fan running.

So the small fan you mean is the power supply's fan. What is it doing?

1. Not spinning at all
2. Spinning, but loud, buzzing or rattling
3. Switching on and off

Please don't open the power supply or poke anything through the grille. If you notice a burning smell, a very hot plug or any sparks, unplug it straight away and tell me.
hi, is thor P2

Thanks, a Thor P2. Then the small fan in your photo is the one on the end of the Thor P2's power supply.

What is that fan doing?

1. Not spinning at all
2. Spinning, but loud, buzzing or rattling
3. Switching on and off

Also, is the miner itself running normally, with the big fan going and hashrate showing in the web UI? A short video with sound would really help me here, especially if it's a noise.
working

Good, so the miner itself is working.

Now just the small fan on the power supply. Is it:

1. Not spinning
2. Spinning but noisy
3. Turning on and off

If it's not spinning while the miner is hashing, please check one thing: carefully hold your hand near the power supply case, without touching the grille. Does it feel warm, or very hot? On many power supplies the fan only starts once the unit warms up, so the answer helps me tell whether this is normal.
mine is working. but the PSU fans not working
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill

Thanks, that's clear: the miner is hashing, but the small fan on the power supply isn't spinning.

That may be normal. On many power supplies the fan only starts once the inside gets warm, and at lower load it can stay off. Your Thor P2 is running fine, so the power supply is still delivering power.

One check so I can tell whether this is normal or a faulty fan:

1. Let the miner run for at least 30 minutes.
2. Hold your hand near the power supply case, without touching the grille, and tell me whether it feels cool, warm or very hot.
3. If you can, send a short video of the fan end of the power supply while the miner is running.

If the case feels very hot (too hot to keep your hand on), or you notice a burning smell, unplug it right away and tell me.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks. This photo shows the power supply from the side, with the barrel cable plugged in and the small fan behind its grille. The blades look sharp, not blurred, so the fan does look stopped at that moment. A still photo can't fully show that, though.

I still need the temperature check to tell whether this is normal:

1. Has the miner been running for at least 30 minutes?
2. Near the power supply case, without touching the grille, does it feel cool, warm or very hot?

A 5 to 10 second video of the fan end, with sound, would settle it.

If it ever feels too hot to keep your hand on, or smells of burning, unplug it straight away and tell me.
i suspect the cover is metal grill is deep inside. so the fans not working

That could well be it. If the grille got pushed in during shipping, it can press on the blades and stop the fan.

Please check it safely:

1. Unplug the power supply from the wall and give it a few minutes to cool.
2. Shine a phone torch through the grille and look from the side. Is the grille bent inward and touching the fan blades?
3. Send me a close-up photo of what you see.

Please don't unscrew the case, bend the grille back or push anything through it. The inside of a power supply can hold a dangerous charge even when it's unplugged.

Until we've sorted this, keep an eye on how hot the case gets while the miner runs. If it feels too hot to keep your hand on, unplug it.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks. In this photo the power supply is unplugged with the AC socket empty, and the whole case is visible from above. From this angle the case and fan grille look straight, with no obvious dent. I can't see whether the grille touches the blades from this far away, though.

Two things would settle it:

1. A close-up straight into the grille with your phone torch on, so I can see the blades and the gap between them and the grille.
2. Earlier, after the miner had been running a while, did the power supply case feel cool, warm or very hot?

Please keep it unplugged while you take the close-up.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Hal again, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist.

Thanks for the photo. It's a little closer, still from above at an angle. The grille sits flat in the end panel, with all four screws in place and no dent or bulge I can see. From this angle I can't see the blades behind it, so I can't yet tell whether anything is touching them.

Two quick things:

1. Hold your phone straight in front of the fan end, lens pointing directly into the grille, with the torch on, and take one photo.
2. After the miner had run for a while, how did the power supply case feel: cool, warm or very hot?

The second answer matters most. If the case stays cool or only slightly warm while mining, the fan may simply not need to spin yet.
this is much clear

Thanks, that's much clearer. It's a straight-on view of the fan end: the figure-8 AC socket on the left, the fan grille on the right, and the yellow output connector on the cable that goes to the miner.

The grille looks fine. It's stamped flat into the end panel, level with the case, with both screws in place. I can't see anything pushed inward, so the grille doesn't look like what's stopping the fan.

That leaves two possibilities: the fan only starts when the power supply gets warm, or the fan itself has failed. One test tells them apart:

1. Plug the power supply back in and let the Thor P2 mine for 30 minutes.
2. Hold your hand near the case without touching the grille. Does it feel cool, warm, or too hot to keep your hand on?
3. Check whether the fan has started spinning.

Tell me what you find. If it's too hot to keep your hand on and the fan still isn't spinning, unplug it and let me know.
